briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Tops $17B as Repeal Push Builds; Nationally, Rescheduling and Psilocybin Momentum Grow
briefs.top: Michigan's legal market just crossed $17 billion in lifetime sales even as the 24% wholesale tax squeezes margins — and a growing repeal coalition, including a gubernatorial candidate, is now making the tax a 2026 campaign issue. Nationally, cannabis rescheduling keeps clearing procedural hurdles while Compass Pathways' psilocybin therapy nears its FDA finish line, giving operators real reasons for optimism heading into Q4.

local.text: Michigan crosses $17 billion in lifetime cannabis sales — the state's combined adult-use and medical market hit the milestone even amid this year's tax headwinds.
Gubernatorial hopeful pledges to kill the 24% wholesale tax — Rep. John James has taken roughly $90,000 from cannabis executives and now says he'll repeal the tax if elected governor.

Rize keeps growing where rivals shut down — the U.P. chain is splitting the wholesale tax burden with suppliers instead of absorbing it alone, even as Higher Love closed five of its nine locations under the same tax.
Jars Cannabis wins surveillance fight in Madison Heights — the 54-store chain got a parking-lot-facing police camera removed after negotiating with the city.
State drops record $2M fine on Muha Meds maker — regulators revoked Michigan Investment 10's processor license over 'egregious violations,' clearing the field for compliant competitors.

national.text: Alabama drops its rescheduling opposition — the state's health department resolved its legal objections, removing one of the last formal holdouts against moving cannabis to Schedule III.
Compass Pathways nears the finish line on psilocybin — the company expects to complete its rolling FDA application for COMP360 in Q4 and still targets a 2027 commercial launch.
Curaleaf goes cross-border with $1.5B Aurora bid — the MSO's takeover offer signals major operators are betting on rescheduling-driven confidence to pursue Canadian consolidation.
Vireo Growth's buying spree keeps expanding — the MSO added an $88.5M New York cultivation complex and a $40M ag-supply company in the same week.
States say DEA is slow-walking rescheduling guidance — California's cannabis director says the agency shows no interest in helping states implement the policy shift.
